title: “Not every person called ‘faithful’ in Scripture was actually faithful to God in the way people assume. Some were sincere, but still wrong. Some were zealous, but still disobedient. Read that again.”
paragraphs: “Not every person called ‘faithful’ in Scripture was actually faithful to God in the way people assume. Some were sincere, but still wrong. Some were zealous, but still disobedient. Read that again.”

Because the Bible does not praise mere religious appearance.
It exposes the heart.

Saul looked committed.
Jonah knew God deeply.
Peter swore loyalty.
The Pharisees built their whole identity on devotion.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

You can look dedicated and still resist God.
You can sound spiritual and still be ruled by pride.
You can be near holy things and still need repentance.
That is exactly why Jesus is everything.

The Bible is not a celebration of human consistency.
It is a revelation of human failure… and God’s mercy in Christ.

The message is not:
“Try harder to be one of the faithful ones.”

The message is:
Even the strongest fall, even the religious can be blind, and even the sincere can be wrong—so run to Jesus.

Because sincerity cannot save you.
Knowledge cannot save you.
Reputation cannot save you.
Only Christ saves.

Sin must be confronted.
Pride must be crucified.
Repentance must be real.
Grace must be received.
And redemption is found in Jesus alone.

That changes how you read the whole Bible.
Not as a museum of flawless believers—
but as a testimony that God rescues broken people who could never rescue themselves.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
